title: DNA Extraction from Zooplankton
author: Andreas Novotny

steps.title: Subset bulk zooplankton sample
steps.instruction: Use a plankton net filter to remove the ethanol preservative (keep the preservative). Resuspend the zooplankton in dH₂O. Use a Fulton splitter to take 1/8 of the original sample and place it into a 50 mL Falcon tube; return the remaining fractions to the ethanol preservative.

steps.title: Pellet zooplankton
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Falcon tube at 5 000 × g for 5 min, discard all supernatant, add sucrose lysis buffer (SLB) to a total volume of 6 mL and resuspend the pellet.

steps.title: Bead‑beating homogenization
steps.instruction: Add three 3.5 mm UFO beads and ~30 small stainless‑steel beads (0.9–2.0 mm) to the tube and vortex vigorously at full speed for at least 10 min, or until no visible zooplankton structures remain.

steps.title: Transfer homogenate to SLB
steps.instruction: Add 1 800 µL SLB to new labeled 15 mL Falcon tubes, then add 100 µL of the homogenized zooplankton (≈1 900 µL total volume).

steps.title: Lysozyme & RNase A digestion
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL lysozyme (125 mg dissolved in 1 000 µL 1× TE) and 20 µL RNase A (10 µg/mL; prepared as 1 µL in 999 µL 1× TE) to each sample tube. Incubate in a rotating incubator at 37 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: Proteinase K & SDS digestion
steps.instruction: Add 100 µL Proteinase K and 100 µL 20 % SDS to each lysate tube. Incubate in a rotating incubator at 55 °C for 1–2 h.

steps.title: Add additional sucrose lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL sucrose lysis buffer (SLB) to each lysate tube.

steps.title: Phenol‑chloroform‑IAA extraction
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, add an equal volume (~3 mL) of phenol:chloroform:IAA (25:24:1, pH 8.0) to the lysate tube, invert by hand for 10 s, then centrifuge at 2 500 g for 6 min (or until the aqueous layer is clear). Wait ≥10 min before opening the centrifuge. Transfer the aqueous (top) layer to a new 15 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Chloroform‑IAA extraction
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (~3 mL) of chloroform:IAA (24:1) to the tube containing the aqueous layer, invert by hand for 10 s, centrifuge at 2 500 g for 6 min (or until the aqueous layer is clear and free of debris). Wait ≥10 min before opening the centrifuge. Transfer the aqueous layer to a labeled Amicon Ultra centrifugal filter (UFC801096, EMD Millipore).

steps.title: Initial Amicon TE wash
steps.instruction: Top up the Amicon filter with 1–2 mL 1× TE buffer and spin at 3 500 g for 10–15 min. Ensure less than 1 mL liquid remains; if more, add 2 mL 1× TE and spin again.

steps.title: TE buffer washes
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL 1× TE to the Amicon filter and spin at 3 500 g for 6 min; discard filtrate. Repeat this wash a total of three times. For the final wash, spin until 200–500 µL remain (≈8–10 min), note the final volume, and transfer the concentrate to a labeled 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube. Rinse the filter sides with 50 µL 1× TE and pool the rinse with the sample in the same tube.

steps.title: Aliquot and store DNA
steps.instruction: Optionally aliquot 50 µL of the final DNA into a 1.5 mL tube as a working stock and store at –20 °C. Store the remaining DNA stock at –80 °C for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration
steps.instruction: Quantify the DNA stock using a Qubit fluorometer according to the manufacturer’s instructions, using 2 µL of DNA stock per assay.

steps.title: Normalize DNA to 2.5 ng/µL
steps.instruction: Using the concentration obtained from Qubit, calculate the volume of DNA stock needed to make 25 µL of a 2.5 ng/µL solution (spreadsheet provided). Add the calculated volume of DNA stock and add nuclease‑free water to reach a total volume of 25 µL, yielding a 2.5 ng/µL DNA stock. Store this normalized stock at –20 °C.
